notes: HomeStop = Shoppers Stop's Home vertical (categoryPath1=Home) on the shared shoppersstop.com marketplace; no separate homestop domain. Access: direct HTTP fetch (ClaudeBot explicitly Allowed in robots.txt except /checkout,/cart,/login,/account,/orders,/payment), parsed Next.js __NEXT_DATA__ (CMS header + CLP page JSON) and queried the site's own Unbxd (Mimir) search index directly (https://search.unbxd.io/.../search) for facets and raw product fields, scoped strictly to categoryPath1_uFilter='Home'. Checked: (1) main nav/mega menu - webCategories top items are MEN/WOMEN/KIDS/WATCHES/BRANDS/HOMESTOP/GIFTS plus Style Hub/Bargains/Luxe; no Bestsellers nav item anywhere. (2) Homestop CLP (/category/homestop) CMS page JSON - its only candidate-looking widget, 'PopularCategories'/'Best Selling Categories' (id 12, componentName 'Best Selling Categories'), is a generic site-wide marketing carousel linking to top-level departments (Men, Women, Makeup categories) - not a Home-scoped Bestsellers listing and not a product PLP at all, so excluded per §3 (marketing banner, not a listing). No other Bestsellers-labelled widget exists on the Homestop CLP (verified the full components array: category-grid, hero-banners, shop-by-budget, deals-card - all generic category/brand links). (3) Unbxd facet list for categoryPath1=Home (categoryPath1/2/3, brand, pro_type, gender, pattern, discountPercent, offer, color_family, fabric, v_size, country_of_origin) has no facet/tag for bestseller/popular/trending. (4) Inspected raw Unbxd product documents directly - schema does contain an 'is_best_seller_checkbox' field, which looked promising, but sampled 500 products across Home AND every other department (Women/Men/Kids/Beauty, 100 each) and it is 'No' on literally every single product checked - a dormant/unused catalog attribute, not an active merchandising tag; filtering on it (Yes/true/1) returned 0 products site-wide. (5) Site's own search for 'bestsellers'/'best sellers' returns either a non-discriminating 16020-result fallback (clearly not a curated concept, no distinct landing page, title stays the generic homepage title) or 0 results - not proof of a genuine PLP either way, treated as unreliable per the false-absence rule, but combined with (1)-(4) it corroborates absence. (6) Brute-force checked guessed URL shapes (/bestsellers, /best-sellers, /best-selling, /top-sellers, /popular, /trending, /home-bestsellers) - all 404. (7) sitemap-plps.xml / sitemap-landingpages.xml live on a separate host (api-ssl.shoppersstop.com) which returned HTTP 503 on two attempts (genuine host-level outage, not a bot block - www.shoppersstop.com itself returned 200 throughout) so could not be cross-checked, but items (1)-(6) already give a consistent, convergent absence signal scoped correctly to Home. Conclusion: no genuine Bestsellers-type merchandising PLP exists for HomeStop/Home on shoppersstop.com.
